domain: EU trademark law / EUIPO opposition-division outcome prediction (case-level likelihood-of-confusion and opposition-outcome task, EU agency publisher)

jurisdiction.publisher: European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO), Alicante

prediction_question: For an opposition filed at EUIPO against an EU trade mark application, will the Opposition Division uphold the opposition (find likelihood of confusion / double identity under Art. 8(1) EUTMR)?
prediction_time: At opposition filing: both marks' text/images, Nice classes and seniority data are public and fixed; the decision follows months later. (Design sketch only - not probed further; the mirror verdict ended the lead.)
target_definition: Binary opposition outcome (upheld vs rejected/partially upheld), from the Opposition Division's published decision. Not constructed.

sources.name: EUIPO eSearch plus / eSearch Case Law (opposition decisions repository) and the prior-art datasets built from it
sources.access: Not probed (mirror verdict found first, at shortlisting). Publisher states: 'All opposition decisions are published online and can be consulted in eSearch plus.'
sources.licence: NOT TRIAGED - the mirror verdict is decisive and precedes any licence reading; no permission may be inferred from this record.

license_evidence: No licence instrument was read: the named prior art already ships the task in scored, released form, so probing (including licence reading) stopped at the decisive verdict, per 'a decisive rejection ends probing'.

measurements.prior_art_measured: Named prior art (all found 2026-11-03, one web search: 'EUIPO opposition decision prediction dataset machine learning trademark'): (1) Haller, M. (2023), 'TrademarkML: predicting the likelihood of confusion', TU Wien - TMSIM-500 dataset of 500 EUIPO opposition cases, publicly released at doi 10.7910/DVN/PNFQLC, with a published ML pipeline and train/test splits ensuring both marks of a case stay in one set; (2) arXiv 2201.01164 'Interpretable Low-Resource Legal Decision Making' - released trademark case-law dataset (~525 lawyer-annotated CJEU + ~2,852 weakly-labelled EUIPO Opposition/Board-of-Appeal decisions drawn from a ~52,000-case pool), RoBERTa scored for likelihood-of-confusion; (3) ICAIL 2023 (ULiege, 'A quantitative evaluation of trademark search engines') - 8,126 EUIPO Opposition Division decisions 2016-2022 assembled as evaluation data; (4) Simmons & Simmons 'Rocketeer' (World Trademark Review, 2023) - commercial ML predictor of EU trademark conflict outcomes trained on ~7,400 EUIPO opposition decisions, reported 93% accuracy.

rejection_reason: Mirror with the precedent named. The task this source most naturally carries - predicting the outcome of an EUIPO opposition / likelihood-of-confusion conflict between two marks - already exists in published, scored, released form: the TMSIM-500 dataset (doi 10.7910/DVN/PNFQLC) with splits and published models, the arXiv 2201.01164 released case-law dataset with RoBERTa scoring, an ICAIL 2023 evaluation over 8,126 EUIPO opposition decisions, and a commercial tool (Rocketeer, 93% reported) trained on 7,400 such decisions. The bench also already publishes a registry-outcome task in the same family (ipo-trademark-registration-outcome, GB, published). Population, target and prediction instant are the same as the released prior art; a different URL or registry interface is not a contribution.
review: Cheapest decisive rejection of the session: the prior-art sweep ran before any EUIPO probing, and the named, released datasets settle the task-level mirror question.
next_action: Closed for the likelihood-of-confusion / opposition-outcome / BoA-affirmance targets (all covered by the named prior art, which included Board of Appeal decisions as augmentation data). Reopen only with a task contract on EUIPO data whose target variable is genuinely different from the released prior art, with its own recorded novelty sweep before any further probing.
